rule: Written before any of these questions was run. The platform must not be changed for any question of this set; a failure here is reported as a failure. Reference numbers are the published abstracts' or results' own numbers; evidence_quality says what was read. Papers were chosen by topic filters in the task brief, excluding the 20 tuning questions and the 27 team questions.

items.question: In patients with community-acquired pneumonia, is aspirin treatment associated with 28-day mortality?
items.citation: Wang G et al., Frontiers in Pharmacology, 2024
items.population_as_in_paper: Community-acquired pneumonia patients in MIMIC-IV (n=3,595)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Aspirin treatment (timing window not stated in abstract; 2,261 received)
items.design_as_in_paper: Propensity score matching; multivariate Cox; secondary 325 vs 81 mg/day comparison
items.main_results: 3,595 included; 1,219 pairs after PSM; 28-day mortality 20.46% in aspirin users; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.63-0.88), p<0.001; 325 vs 81 mg: no mortality difference, ICU stay 4.22 vs 3.57 d (p=0.031)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Exposure window not stated in abstract; CAP definition by diagnosis codes; aspirin dose sub-analysis unsupported
items.notes: Candidate was in seed list; verified.  Aspirin class count 1. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In ICU patients with acute respiratory failure, is metformin use associated with in-hospital mortality?
items.citation: Yang Y et al., Frontiers in Pharmacology, 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: ICU patients with acute respiratory failure, MIMIC-IV
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Metformin use (timing not stated in abstract)
items.outcome_as_in_paper: In-hospital and ICU mortality (primary); 30-day and 90-day mortality (secondary)
items.design_as_in_paper: PSM, Cox, logistic regression, machine-learning feature selection for confounders
items.main_results: After PSM 1,429 pts (374 metformin, 1,055 non-users); in-hospital mortality OR 0.202 (0.123-0.317); ICU mortality OR 0.245 (0.142-0.399); 30-day HR 0.199 (0.124-0.320); 90-day HR 0.230 (0.150-0.352)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Metformin is largely a home drug; abstract does not say whether in-hospital or pre-admission use; very large effect suggests immortal-time/indication bias
items.notes: Implausibly large effect size; useful as a test of whether the platform flags exposure timing. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In adults with sepsis, is prophylactic proton pump inhibitor use associated with 28- and 90-day all-cause mortality?
items.citation: Ma C et al., Frontiers in Pharmacology, 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: Adult sepsis (Sepsis-3) patients in MIMIC-IV, n=18,198
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Prophylactic PPI use
items.outcome_as_in_paper: All-cause mortality 28-90 days (primary); in-hospital and ICU mortality, hospital/ICU stay, adverse events (secondary)
items.design_as_in_paper: Stepwise Cox regression, prediction models (ROC), Kaplan-Meier
items.main_results: 18,198 sepsis patients; prophylactic PPI use significantly associated with increased 90-day mortality (p<0.001); PPI did not improve 28- or 90-day survival; ICU stay about 1 day shorter, hospital stay not shorter. No HR/CI in abstract.
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Abstract gives no HR/CI so reference numbers are weak; fetch full text (probably PMC12223537) before using as numeric target
items.notes: Seed candidate PMC12223537 could not be opened (PMC returns a bot-check page); this PMID is the matching MIMIC-IV prophylactic-PPI sepsis paper, not confirmed identical to the PMC ID. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In patients with ARDS, is early prophylactic heparin use associated with in-hospital mortality?
items.citation: Xiao LX et al., Journal of Intensive Care, 2024
items.population_as_in_paper: ARDS patients in MIMIC-IV
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Prophylactic heparin within the first 72 h of ICU admission
items.design_as_in_paper: PSM and inverse probability weighting; Cox; doubly robust models
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Few; 72 h window is longer than the usual 24-48 h
items.notes: Replaces seed PMC10895755 (not openable); this is likely the same paper family but ID not confirmed. Heparin class count 1. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In patients with sepsis, is hydrocortisone treatment associated with 90-day mortality?
items.citation: Li M et al., Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy, 2024
items.population_as_in_paper: Sepsis patients in MIMIC-IV, 2008-2019 (n=31,749)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Hydrocortisone received after sepsis diagnosis
items.outcome_as_in_paper: 90-day mortality; survivors' hospital length of stay
items.design_as_in_paper: Propensity score matching (indication and contraindication factors); Cox HR
items.main_results: 1,802 hydrocortisone patients vs 6,348 matched non-users; 90-day mortality HR 1.35 (1.24-1.47); in-hospital mortality 40.9% vs 27.6% (p<0.0001); hospital stay in survivors median 12.6 vs 10.8 d
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Exposure is 'after diagnosis' (time-varying/landmark); strong confounding by indication
items.notes: Seed candidate; verified. Steroid class count 1 (plus H-A09). Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In ICU patients with delirium, is haloperidol use associated with 28-day mortality?
items.citation: Chen C et al., Internal Medicine Journal, 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: ICU patients diagnosed with delirium on first ICU admission, MIMIC-IV 2008-2022 (n=9,109)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Haloperidol treatment (1,359 treated)
items.outcome_as_in_paper: 28-day and in-hospital mortality; ICU and hospital stay
items.design_as_in_paper: 1:1 PSM (caliper 0.05; 1,323 pairs); Cox; KM; subgroups
items.main_results: Before PSM 28-day mortality 15.08% vs 26.79%; in-hospital 13.76% vs 23.38%; after PSM 28-day HR 0.65 (0.54-0.78), in-hospital HR 0.69 (0.57-0.83); longer ICU stay 8.10 vs 5.81 d (unmatched)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Delirium diagnosis code is mostly assigned late/after drug; haloperidol timing window not stated in abstract
items.notes: Antipsychotic. Strong immortal-time/indication risk, good stress test. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In cirrhotic patients, is early unfractionated heparin use associated with 30-day mortality?
items.citation: Guo M et al., Turkish Journal of Gastroenterology, 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: Cirrhotic patients in MIMIC-IV with ICU admission (n=1,652)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Unfractionated heparin within 48 h after ICU admission (781 early heparin)
items.design_as_in_paper: Kaplan-Meier, Cox, logistic regression, PSM sensitivity
items.main_results: 1,652 cirrhotic pts (781 vs 871); 30-day mortality HR 0.742 (0.599-0.919), p=0.006; after PSM HR 0.729 (0.568-0.937), p=0.014; transfusion OR 0.917 (0.693-1.215) before and 0.857 (0.616-1.191) after PSM
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Secondary outcome (transfusion) is a procedure not in outcome list; UFH vs LMWH not distinguished beyond UFH
items.notes: Heparin class count 2 (with H-A04). Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In critically ill adults with acute ischemic stroke, is early acetaminophen use associated with 30- and 90-day mortality?
items.citation: Wang X et al., Scientific Reports, 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: Critically ill adults with acute ischemic stroke, MIMIC-IV 2008-2019 (n=1,779); eICU validation (n=1,182)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Acetaminophen within 48 h of ICU admission
items.design_as_in_paper: Target trial emulation with clone-censor-weight; sensitivity, competing-risk and subgroup analyses
items.main_results: 90-day mortality HR 0.70 (0.58-0.84), p<0.001; 30-day HR 0.66 (0.54-0.81); benefit most apparent in patients without diabetes
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Clone-censor-weight method is not a standard cohort comparison; question itself is simple
items.notes: Analytical method is beyond the platform but the question wording is simple; use to see how the platform handles a result with a different design. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In adults with septic shock, how do methylprednisolone and hydrocortisone compare for 30-day mortality?
items.citation: Xu J, Cai H, Zheng X, BMC Infectious Diseases, 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults with septic shock, MIMIC-IV v3.0 (n=1,607; overall 30-day mortality 42.1%)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Methylprednisolone received after diagnosis
items.design_as_in_paper: 1:1 PSM (376 pairs); Cox; subgroup and sensitivity analyses
items.main_results: 30-day mortality 141/376 (37.5%) vs 131/376 (34.8%), HR 1.105 (0.871-1.402), P=0.410; methylprednisolone: longer ICU stay, higher glucose, shorter vasopressin duration
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Few; head-to-head two-drug comparison with null result
items.notes: Seed candidate; abstract read. Steroid class count 2 (with H-A05). Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, how do propofol, midazolam and their combination compare for 30-day mortality?
items.citation: Zheng J et al., Journal of Surgical Research, 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: Sepsis-associated AKI patients in MIMIC-IV (n=3,335)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Sedation strategy: propofol alone, midazolam alone, or both
items.comparator_as_in_paper: No sedation / propofol monotherapy as reference
items.design_as_in_paper: Kaplan-Meier, Cox, IPTW; subgroup and mediation analyses
items.main_results: Versus propofol alone: midazolam alone HR 1.945 (1.519-2.490); combination HR 1.573 (1.275-1.942); IPTW HR 1.742 and 1.328
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Sedation tied to mechanical ventilation; mediation analysis (metabolic acidosis) not needed; three-way comparison plus a no-sedation group
items.notes: Seed candidate; verified. Sedative class count 1. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In adults with sepsis, how do empirical piperacillin/tazobactam and cefepime compare for 90-day mortality?
items.citation: Lee Y et al., Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: Adult sepsis patients in MIMIC-IV who received either antibiotic empirically (n=2,485)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Empirical piperacillin/tazobactam (n=1,161)
items.outcome_as_in_paper: 90-day mortality; C. difficile infection; VRE colonization
items.design_as_in_paper: Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting; Kaplan-Meier
items.main_results: No significant 90-day mortality difference after stabilized IPTW; log-rank P=0.947; no difference in C. difficile infection or VRE colonization (no HR/CI in abstract)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: 'Empirical' timing window not defined in abstract; abstract gives no HR so numeric target must come from full text
items.notes: New candidate (antibiotic head-to-head). Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In adults with septic shock, how do norepinephrine plus phenylephrine and norepinephrine plus vasopressin compare for in-hospital mortality?
items.citation: Dong Y et al., International Journal of Surgery, 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: Septic shock patients in MIMIC-IV 2008-2019 (n=753: NE-PE 238, NE-VP 515); eICU validation n=313
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Norepinephrine + phenylephrine as second vasopressor
items.outcome_as_in_paper: In-hospital mortality (also duration of dual vasopressor therapy)
items.design_as_in_paper: 1:1 PSM (168 pairs) and stabilized IPTW; logistic regression; interaction with Shock Index
items.main_results: NE-PE had lower in-hospital mortality than NE-VP in PSM, IPTW and multivariable analysis (exact rates and ORs not given in abstract); effect larger in age <65 and no hypertension
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Drug combinations and sequence (second-line add-on) are hard to define; abstract has no numeric effect sizes
items.notes: Numbers must be taken from the full text before use. Vasopressor class count 1. Abstract text read via Europe PMC REST record (PubMed/PMC pages blocked or redirected); full text not read.

items.question: In adults with sepsis, is the platelet count in the first 24 hours of ICU admission associated with 28-day mortality?
items.citation: Wang D, Wang S, Wu H, et al. Association Between Platelet Levels and 28-Day Mortality in Patients With Sepsis: A Retrospective Analysis of a Large Clinical Database MIMIC-IV. Front Med 2022;9:833996
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults >=18 y with sepsis, ICU admission, MIMIC-IV 2008-2019; excluded SOFA <2 and no vitals/platelet count; n=16,401
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Platelet count within 24 h of ICU admission (lowest value kept), x10^9/L: <50 (n=884), 50-100 (n=2,396), 100-150 (n=4,423, reference), >=150 (n=8,698)
items.outcome_as_in_paper: 28-day mortality (secondary: ICU and hospital length of stay)
items.design_as_in_paper: Cox models, 3 nested adjustment models (demographics/BMI; + comorbidities, infection source; + ventilation, RRT, SAPS II, labs, vitals); GAM and two-piece linear threshold regression; multiple imputation
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Four-level category with non-reference middle group; non-linear threshold (two-piece); sepsis cohort with SOFA>=2 restriction; adjustment includes SAPS II
items.notes: Paper has internal inconsistencies (text counts differ slightly from Table 1; P-trend 0.262 in text vs 0.041 in table; abstract says 1% per 10 units vs 13% wording). Use Table 3 Model 3 numbers.

items.question: In adults with sepsis, is the blood urea nitrogen to albumin ratio in the first 24 hours of ICU admission associated with 30-day mortality?
items.citation: Wang Y, Gao S, Hong L, et al. Prognostic impact of blood urea nitrogen to albumin ratio on patients with sepsis: a retrospective cohort study. Sci Rep 2023;13:10013
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults with sepsis (Sepsis-3) at ICU admission, first ICU admission only, MIMIC-IV v2.0; n=7,656
items.exposure_as_in_paper: BUN/albumin ratio (mg/g), first values within 24 h of ICU admission; dichotomised at cohort median 8.0 (<=8.0 n=3,837; >8.0 n=3,819)
items.design_as_in_paper: Cox univariate, Model I (age, sex), Model II (vitals, comorbidities, labs, SOFA, SAPS II); KM; ROC vs SOFA/BUN/albumin; subgroups
items.main_results: 30-day mortality 28.6% overall; 19.1% (low BAR) vs 38.2% (high). HR high vs low: univariate 2.272 (2.079-2.483); Model I 2.071 (1.892-2.267); Model II 1.219 (1.095-1.357). 360-day Model II HR 1.263 (1.159-1.376). AUC 30-day: BAR 0.661, SOFA 0.703
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Ratio of two labs; median split; adjustment set includes SOFA and SAPS II; AUC comparison not a platform output
items.notes: Covariate lists in Methods and Table 2 footnote do not fully match (per fetched text). PMC page itself blocked by captcha; text read via Europe PMC XML of the same paper.

items.question: In critically ill adults with pneumonia, is the glucose-to-platelet ratio in the first 24 hours of ICU admission associated with 30-day mortality?
items.citation: Zhang W, Liu X, Li Z, et al. Association between the glucose-to-platelet ratio and short-term and long-term all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with pneumonia: a retrospective cohort study. J Thorac Dis 2026;18(4):333
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults >=18 y, ICU admission with pneumonia (ICD-9/10), first ICU stay, MIMIC-IV v3.1; excluded ICU stay <24 h and missing glucose/platelet in first 24 h; n=9,817
items.exposure_as_in_paper: GPR = glucose (mg/dL) / platelet (x10^9/L), first 24 h; continuous and tertiles T1 0.19-0.55, T2 0.55-0.88, T3 0.88-3.11
items.design_as_in_paper: Cox, 3 models (unadjusted; age, sex, race, weight; + chronic pulmonary disease, norepinephrine, ventilation, DBP, SpO2, WBC, creatinine, INR, urine output); RCS 4 knots; trend test; subgroups; random-forest multiple imputation
items.main_results: Deaths 2,004 (20.4%) at 30 d, 3,860 (39.3%) at 360 d. 30-day Model 3: per unit HR 1.12 (1.10-1.15); T2 vs T1 HR 1.05 (0.93-1.17); T3 vs T1 HR 1.37 (1.23-1.53); P trend <0.001; nonlinearity P=0.047. Crude 30-day mortality by tertile 18%, 19%, 25%. AUC not reported
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Ratio of two labs; tertiles; adjustment includes drug and ventilation flags; spline nonlinearity
items.notes: Published 2026 (J Thorac Dis). Pneumonia identified by diagnosis code. The earlier candidate described as 30-day was confirmed as this paper.

items.question: In critically ill adults with acute myocardial infarction, is arterial lactate in the first 24 hours of ICU admission associated with hospital mortality?
items.citation: Lu T, Tan L, Xu K, et al. Outcomes of hyperlactatemia on admission in critically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction: A retrospective study from MIMIC-IV. Front Endocrinol 2022;13:1015298
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults with AMI and ICU admission, MIMIC-IV v2.0 (2008-2019), first ICU stay, with lactate in first 24 h; n=2,171 (of 3,324 AMI ICU patients)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: First arterial lactate within 24 h of ICU admission: <=2 (n=1,187, ref), >2-5 (n=780), >5-10 (n=155), >10 mmol/L (n=49)
items.design_as_in_paper: Logistic regression (hospital mortality) and Cox (time-to-death); covariates by univariable screen incl. APS III, SOFA, SIRS, vasoactive drugs; KM; subgroups by cardiogenic shock and acute heart failure
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Clinical cut-point categories (not quartiles); multiple outcome horizons; adjustment includes APS III and SIRS (SIRS count may not be computed); subgroup interaction
items.notes: Text gives group III CI as 2.15-35.58 but abstract/Table 2 give 2.15-5.58 (typo in text). Lactate is used in 2 further items (H-B10 delirium, H-B11 SA-AKI), exceeding the 2-per-marker cap: drop one of them if a strict cap is needed.

items.question: In critically ill adults with non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage, is serum sodium within 24 hours of admission associated with ICU and in-hospital mortality?
items.citation: Liu J, Li J, Zhang Q, et al. Association between serum sodium levels within 24 h of admission and all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage: a retrospective analysis of the MIMIC-IV database. Front Neurol 2023;14:1234080
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults >18 y with non-traumatic SAH, MIMIC-IV v2.0, first ICU admission, sodium within 24 h, ICU stay >=24 h, <=5% missing; n=864
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Serum sodium within 24 h of admission: continuous (per 1 mmol/L) and <135 (n=39), 135-145 (n=691, ref), >=145 mmol/L (n=134); threshold analysis
items.outcome_as_in_paper: ICU all-cause mortality and in-hospital all-cause mortality
items.design_as_in_paper: Cox; Model I age, sex, race; Model II + vitals, GCS, SAPS II, APS III, comorbidities, labs (WBC, platelets, Hb, glucose, BUN, creatinine, bicarbonate, chloride); KM; two-segment threshold; subgroups
items.main_results: ICU mortality 32.6% (282/864); hospital mortality 19.2% (166/864). Continuous Model II: ICU HR 1.05 (1.03-1.08), hospital HR 1.09 (1.06-1.12). >=145 vs 135-145: ICU HR 1.47 (1.07-2.01), hospital HR 2.26 (1.54-3.32). <135: not significant. J-shaped, inflection ~141 mmol/L (above: ICU HR 1.098, hospital HR 1.155)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Non-linear J-shape with threshold; small population (SAH); adjustment includes GCS, SAPS II and APS III (APS III not computed); two outcomes
items.notes: Methods mention logistic regression but results use Cox; threshold 141 vs category cut-point 145 (per fetched text).

items.question: In critically ill adults with acute kidney injury, is glycemic variability on the first day of ICU admission associated with 30-day ICU mortality?
items.citation: Guo Y, Qiu Y, et al. Association between glycemic variability and short-term mortality in patients with acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study of the MIMIC-IV database. Sci Rep 2024;14:5945
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults >=18 y with KDIGO AKI within 48 h of admission, first ICU admission, MIMIC-IV v2.1; excluded <3 glucose measurements on ICU day 1 and ICU stay <24 h; n=6,777
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Mean blood glucose (tertiles <125.0, 125.0-167.2, >=167.2 mg/dL) and glucose coefficient of variation (SD/mean; tertiles <12.7, 12.7-24.8, >=24.8%), all values on ICU day 1; also per SD
items.design_as_in_paper: Cox, 4 models up to AKI stage, RRT, ventilation, vasopressors, hypoglycemic drugs, SOFA, comorbidity index; RCS and inflection analysis; multiple imputation; complete-case sensitivity
items.main_results: 30-day ICU mortality 23.5% (1,593/6,777). Model 4 per SD: MBG HR 1.20 (1.14-1.27); CV HR 1.08 (1.03-1.13). CV T3 vs T1 HR 1.37 (1.21-1.56); MBG T3 vs T1 HR 1.34 (1.17-1.53). MBG U-shaped, inflection 111.3 mg/dL; CV linear
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Variability metric (CV of day-1 glucose) needs >=3 measurements; AKI definition (KDIGO within 48 h); two exposures in one paper; U-shaped non-linear mean glucose
items.notes: Only first 100,000 characters of the page were read; headline numbers are from the abstract/results portion. Cohort counts in Methods and Results are not reconciled in the paper. Covers the 'MAGE/glycemic variability' candidate only in spirit: this is CV, not MAGE.

items.question: In ICU patients with diastolic heart failure, is mean body temperature in the first 24 hours associated with 28-day ICU mortality and in-hospital mortality?
items.citation: Xu H, Xie Y, Sun X, Feng N. Association between first 24-h mean body temperature and mortality in patients with diastolic heart failure in intensive care unit: A retrospective cohort study. Front Med 2022;9:1028122
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults >18 y with diastolic heart failure (ICD-9 4283x / ICD-10 I503x), first ICU admission, temperature data in first 24 h, ICU stay >=24 h, MIMIC-IV; n=4,153 of 7,397
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Mean body temperature over first 24 h of ICU: per 1 C, and hypothermia <36.5 (n=980), normal 36.5-<37.5 (n=2,875, ref), hyperthermia >=37.5 C (n=298)
items.design_as_in_paper: Logistic regression, 3 models (demographics; + labs; + HR, SBP, RR, SpO2, Charlson index); RCS (non-linearity P<0.001); subgroups; multiple imputation
items.main_results: 28-day ICU mortality 517/4,153 (12.4%); in-hospital 795 (19.1%). Model 3 per +1 C: OR 0.79 (0.66-0.96) ICU, OR 0.77 (0.66-0.91) hospital. Hypothermia vs normal: OR 1.3 (1.03-1.65) ICU, OR 1.31 (1.07-1.59) hospital. Hyperthermia not significant (OR 1.3, 0.88-1.93; OR 1.13, 0.81-1.57)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Mean of charted temperature over 24 h (vital sign, not lab); U-shape handled by categories; population defined by a specific diagnosis code set; Charlson adjustment
items.notes: Temperature measurement site unclear per authors. Only first 100,000 characters read.

items.question: In adults with sepsis in the ICU, is the absolute lymphocyte count at ICU admission associated with 28-day mortality?
items.citation: Zhong D, Zhao L. Impact of absolute lymphocyte count upon admission to ICU on 28-day mortality in sepsis patients in ICU. Front Immunol 2025;16:1688451 (epub 5 Jan 2026 per PMC)
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults 18-90 y, first ICU admission, Sepsis-3, MIMIC-IV v2.0; excluded HIV, SLE, immunosuppressant use, and no admission lymphocyte count; n=10,263 (from 30,167)
items.exposure_as_in_paper: First absolute lymphocyte count after ICU admission (x10^9/L) in tertiles: low n=3,484 (median 0.46), medium n=3,368 (1.07), high n=3,411 (2.04); also continuous
items.design_as_in_paper: Cox univariable then multivariable (age, weight, SOFA, WBC, Hb, neutrophils, platelets, K, lactate, BUN, creatinine, sex, comorbidities incl. AKI, CKD, COPD, HF, cirrhosis, diabetes); RCS; ROC; median imputation
items.main_results: 28-day deaths 2,125/10,263 (20.71%); by tertile 28.53%, 19.18%, 14.22%. Multivariable HR vs low: medium 0.727 (0.658-0.804); high 0.581 (0.517-0.652). Continuous univariable HR 0.999 (0.993-1.005). AUC FALC 0.604, SOFA 0.715. RCS non-linear P<0.001, risk rises below ~1 x10^9/L
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Count of admission lymphocytes (needs differential); non-linear; large exclusion from missing differential; adjustment includes SOFA and many labs
items.notes: Paper is internally inconsistent (quartile vs tertile wording, threshold 0.755 vs 1, SOFA AUC CI). Only first 100,000 characters read. Date is 2025/2026.

items.question: In ICU patients with acute myocardial infarction and no overt bleeding, is an in-hospital drop in hemoglobin from admission associated with 180-day mortality?
items.citation: Li P, Chen M, Huang Y, et al. Prognostic impact of in-hospital hemoglobin decline in non-overt bleeding ICU patients with acute myocardial infarction. BMC Cardiovasc Disord 2023;23:231
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults with AMI in ICU, no overt bleeding (e.g., no GI bleeding), first ICU stay, ICU stay >=24 h, hemoglobin available, MIMIC-IV 2008-2019; n=2,334
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Hemoglobin drop = admission hemoglobin minus lowest in-hospital value (positive only), g/dL: none n=271; minimal <3 n=1,661; minor 3-<5 n=284; major >=5 n=118; also continuous
items.design_as_in_paper: Time-dependent Cox models (step function), adjusted for demographics, vitals, labs, PCI, baseline hemoglobin, GRACE-related factors; RCS nonlinear analysis; multiple imputation
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Change (admission minus in-hospital nadir) is the exposure, not an outcome; exposure window spans whole stay (immortal-time issue; paper uses time-dependent Cox); non-overt-bleeding exclusion needs diagnosis logic
items.notes: Fits 'change-in-measurement' only loosely: change is the exposure. Model 1 vs Model 2 HRs differ in the paper's tables (11.79/13.90 vs 12.68/13.87). Only first 100,000 characters read.

items.question: In adult ICU patients, is lactate clearance between the first 24 hours and later in the ICU stay associated with delirium?
items.citation: Qian X, Sheng Y, Jiang Y, Xu Y. Associations of serum lactate and lactate clearance with delirium in the early stage of ICU: a retrospective cohort study of the MIMIC-IV database. Front Neurol 2024;15:1371827
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults >=18 y, first ICU admission, ICU stay >1 day, lactate measured at 0-24 h (T0) and after 24 h (T1), no coma/delirium in first 24 h; excluded dementia, psychoses, TBI, nervous system disease, alcohol/drug abuse; n=7,812 of 53,569
items.exposure_as_in_paper: Lactate at T0 and T1 (normal <2; hyperlactatemia 2-5 with pH >7.35; lactic acidosis >5 with pH <7.35); lactate clearance = (T0-T1)/T0 x100%, categories <0, 0-50%, >50%
items.outcome_as_in_paper: Delirium after 24 h (RASS then CAM-ICU); 30-day mortality among delirium patients
items.design_as_in_paper: Logistic regression (OR) for delirium, 3 models; Cox for 30-day mortality; subgroups; VIF check
items.main_results: 30-day mortality 1,903 (24.36%) in full cohort. Delirium Model 3: lactic acidosis at T0 OR 1.235 (1.105-1.382); clearance per 1% OR 0.919 (0.873-0.967); clearance >50% vs <0 OR 0.705 (0.613-0.811). Delirium 30-day HR clearance >50% 0.638 (0.543-0.750)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Change between two lactate draws (T0, T1 timing varies); delirium outcome needs CAM-ICU/RASS charting; pH conditions in categories; very high exclusion rate
items.notes: Abstract delirium prevalence 8.19% (4,338) is inconsistent with n=7,812 (55.5%); text OR values match Model 2 not Model 3 in places. Change is the exposure, not an outcome. Lactate is the 2nd of 3 lactate papers in this file.

items.question: How well can in-hospital death be predicted in adults with heart failure from age, respiratory rate, blood gas, platelet, albumin, bilirubin, lactate and similar baseline values?
items.citation: Development and validation of a novel combinatorial nomogram model to predict in-hospital deaths in heart failure patients. BMC Cardiovasc Disord 2024;24:16
items.population_as_in_paper: Adults 18-90 with heart failure by ICD code, <=20% missing; 16,908 patients (9,427 MIMIC-IV, 7,481 MIMIC-III); 2,283 in-hospital deaths (13.5%)
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: LR1 (11): age, respiratory rate, PaO2, platelets, albumin, total bilirubin, ALP, lactate, pH, base excess, phosphorus; LR2 = LR1 + acute kidney injury + ventricular arrhythmias
items.design_as_in_paper: Logistic regression nomograms (plus LASSO comparison); developed in MIMIC-IV, tested in MIMIC-III
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Needs blood-gas/lab item mapping and a 2-level (with/without AKI, arrhythmia) predictor set; MIMIC-III validation not reproducible (MIMIC-IV only).

items.question: Can 28-day mortality after ICU discharge be predicted in patients with sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy from severity score, age, comorbidity index, lactate and a few labs?
items.citation: Li X et al. Enhancing prognostic accuracy in sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a machine learning approach. Eur J Med Res 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 1,068 adults with sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy, MIMIC-IV; 236 (22.1%) died within 28 days of ICU discharge
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: 7 predictors: APS III, age, Charlson index, cerebrovascular disease, ALP, lactate, CK-MB (selected by Boruta, LASSO, RFECV)
items.design_as_in_paper: 8 ML algorithms compared; final model logistic regression; train/validation/test
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Cohort definition (sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy) is a composite; outcome is post-discharge death window; selection from many candidates.

items.question: How well do routine ICU admission variables predict in-hospital death in ICU patients with catheter-associated urinary tract infection?
items.citation: Liu L et al. Predicting mortality in intensive care unit patients with CAUTI using an interpretable machine learning model. Front Med 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 545 ICU patients with catheter-associated UTI, MIMIC-IV; mortality 7.89% (43/545)
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: 13 SHAP-ranked predictors incl. vasoactive drug use, shock index, APS III, concomitant malignancy
items.outcome_as_in_paper: ICU patient mortality (as stated in abstract: mortality)
items.design_as_in_paper: 4 models compared; logistic regression best
items.main_results: Logistic regression AUC 0.871 (no CI in abstract); 43 events
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Small n and 43 events; CAUTI cohort needs ICD/culture definition; exact mortality window not confirmed from abstract.

items.question: Can acute kidney injury be predicted in patients with acute pancreatitis from baseline clinical variables?
items.citation: Chen F et al. Risk factors for acute kidney injury in patients with acute pancreatitis and construction of nomogram model. Front Med 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 754 acute pancreatitis patients from MIMIC-IV (random train/internal validation); 202 external patients from a Chinese hospital
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: 6 independent risk factors (names not in abstract)
items.design_as_in_paper: Univariate + multivariate logistic regression, nomogram, calibration, DCA
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Predictor names unknown from abstract; platform must pick its own; external cohort not reproducible; AKI definition (KDIGO timing).

items.question: Is the association between red cell distribution width and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with acute cholangitis different between men and women?
items.citation: Liu J et al. Sex differences in the association between red cell distribution width and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with acute cholangitis. BMC Gastroenterol 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 756 critically ill acute cholangitis patients, MIMIC-IV; 146 deaths within 30 days
items.design_as_in_paper: Retrospective cohort, Cox regression with sex interaction/subgroup
items.main_results: Adjusted HR 1.08 (1.01-1.15) per RDW; sex interaction P = 0.007; stronger in males
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Small cohort; sex-stratified HR needs enough events; cholangitis ICD cohort.

items.question: Is early ondansetron use associated with lower 30-day mortality in ventilated ARDS patients, and does the association depend on dose, age or sex?
items.citation: Ji Q et al. Association of early ondansetron use with 30-day mortality in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome. J Thorac Dis 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 6,457 ARDS patients on mechanical ventilation, MIMIC-IV; 1,125 deaths at 30 days
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Early ondansetron use; daily dose (low-dose); age, sex, ARDS severity subgroups
items.design_as_in_paper: Retrospective cohort, propensity score matching, dose and subgroup analyses
items.main_results: Overall HR 0.77 (0.63-0.94); low-dose daily HR 0.67 (0.54-0.83); age>=65 HR 0.54 (0.43-0.67); female HR 0.77 (0.61-0.97), male HR 0.58 (0.47-0.72). Interaction P values not in abstract
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Defining 'early' use window and daily dose from prescriptions/inputevents; ARDS cohort definition; no interaction P to compare, subgroup HRs only.

items.question: Is acetaminophen use associated with lower 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with pulmonary embolism, and is the effect partly mediated by body temperature?
items.citation: Wang X et al. Association between acetaminophen use and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with pulmonary embolism. Front Pharmacol 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 1,983 ICU patients with pulmonary embolism, MIMIC-IV; 599 matched pairs
items.design_as_in_paper: Retrospective cohort, propensity score matching, mediation analysis
items.main_results: HR 0.69 (0.56-0.85) after matching; body temperature mediated 54.2% (25.6%-187.5%)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Mediation with wide CI; mediator timing (temperature after drug); pulmonary embolism cohort definition. Mediation figure read from a Europe PMC summary and the PMC abstract record, not full text.

items.question: Does the association between the triglyceride-glucose index and acute kidney injury in critically ill coronary artery disease patients differ by use of antidiabetic or lipid-lowering drugs?
items.citation: Yang Y et al. Antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapy modify the association between triglyceride-glucose index and acute kidney injury in critically ill patients with coronary artery disease. Front Endocrinol 2025
items.population_as_in_paper: 2,517 critically ill CAD patients, MIMIC-IV; median age 69, 68.06% male
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: TyG index; effect modifiers: antidiabetic drugs, lipid-lowering drugs
items.design_as_in_paper: Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline, interaction tests
items.main_results: TyG OR 2.021 (1.674-2.454) without vs 1.480 (1.190-1.853) with antidiabetics, P interaction 0.040; lipid-lowering P interaction 0.332; RCS linear
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Effect modifier is a drug class, not sex/age (weaker fit to T7 sex/age); in-hospital drug exposure timing vs AKI onset; TyG needs glucose+triglyceride.

items.question: Is starting sertraline instead of citalopram or escitalopram in hospital associated with fewer ECG safety events within 7 days?
items.citation: Lin J et al. Short-term ECG safety after inpatient initiation of sertraline versus citalopram or escitalopram: an observational target-trial emulation using MIMIC-IV-ECG. Gen Hosp Psychiatry 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: 4,921 adults starting sertraline or citalopram/escitalopram, MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-ECG
items.design_as_in_paper: Target-trial emulation
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform must notice outcome comes from ECG machine measurements/waveform files, not tables it holds.
items.out_of_scope_reason: Outcome is measured on ECG recordings (MIMIC-IV-ECG waveform/machine-read data), which the platform does not have; also a target-trial causal framing.

items.question: Is dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor exposure before admission associated with different liver marker trends and death in septic adults with type 2 diabetes compared with metformin?
items.citation: Hepatic biomarker trajectories and mortality in septic adults with type 2 diabetes and recorded DPP-4 inhibitor exposure versus metformin-based therapy: a propensity-score-matched cohort study. Metabolism Open 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: Septic adults with type 2 diabetes, MIMIC-IV; 105 DPP-4 vs 297 metformin patients
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Recorded DPP-4 inhibitor vs metformin-based therapy (abstract notes a pre-admission exposure record present in 60.0%)
items.outcome_as_in_paper: Hepatic biomarker trajectories (bilirubin slope); in-hospital mortality
items.design_as_in_paper: Propensity-score-matched cohort
items.main_results: Bilirubin slope +0.048 mg/dL/day (p=0.221); in-hospital mortality 21.0% vs 13.5%, RR 1.56 (0.97-2.49)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform must recognise exposure is a home/pre-admission drug record, not inpatient administration.
items.out_of_scope_reason: Exposure is based on pre-admission (home/outpatient) medication records, which the platform cannot use; only inpatient drug administration is in scope.

items.question: What glucocorticoid dosing strategy should be recommended for patients with sepsis?
items.citation: Zhang Y et al. Optimization of glucocorticoid administration in patients with sepsis using reinforcement learning: a multicenter retrospective study. Front Cell Infect Microbiol 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: 3,070 MIMIC-IV sepsis patients; 372 eICU-CRD patients for external validation
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Time-varying glucocorticoid dosing decisions (offline RL, CQL policy)
items.outcome_as_in_paper: Expected return of learned policy vs clinician policy
items.design_as_in_paper: Offline reinforcement learning, external validation in eICU
items.main_results: CQL policy had higher expected return than clinician practice in both datasets (no single headline number in abstract); n 3,070 and 372
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform must refuse a treatment-policy recommendation phrased as a plain 'what should be given' question.
items.out_of_scope_reason: Asks for an optimal time-varying treatment strategy (reinforcement learning / dynamic treatment regime) and a treatment recommendation, a causal-policy claim the platform does not make; also uses eICU.

items.question: Can an in-hospital death prediction model for children with sepsis be built from first-day ICU data and tested in other hospitals?
items.citation: Lin J et al. Predicting in-hospital mortality in pediatric sepsis: machine learning development and multicenter validation. J Inflamm Res 2026
items.population_as_in_paper: Pediatric sepsis ICU patients (development cohort; external: pediatric PIC database and adult MIMIC-IV cohort)
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: First-24-hour ICU data; key predictors pH, fibrinogen, lactate, platelets, urea, chloride
items.design_as_in_paper: 8 ML models, XGBoost best; external validation
items.main_results: Development AUC 0.821 (0.751-0.892); external AUC 0.735 (PIC), 0.778 (MIMIC-IV)
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform must refuse on population (children) and other-hospital data rather than run it on adult MIMIC-IV.
items.out_of_scope_reason: Target population is children (paediatric sepsis) with data from a paediatric database (PIC) at another hospital; the platform covers adults in MIMIC-IV only.
